prompt_text: Who is the best marketing agency in Maryland?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” marketing agency for every company — the right one depends on your industry, goals, budget, geography, and preferred working style. I can help you find the best fit. To narrow it down quickly, tell me a few things (or read the steps below and I’ll do the searching for you):

Quick questions
- What kind of marketing do you need? (digital ads, SEO, social media, PR, branding, B2B demand gen, content, web design, integrated)
- Industry or target audience (healthcare, tech/SaaS, retail, professional services, nonprofits, etc.)
- Monthly/annual budget range
- Do you need a local Maryland agency or are remote/nearby firms okay?
- Any timeline or specific KPIs you must hit?

How to pick the “best” agency (fast checklist)
1. Define goals and KPIs up front (sales, leads, CAC, LTV, brand awareness, app installs, etc.).  
2. Look for relevant case studies showing measurable results in your industry or similar company size.  
3. Check reviews and rankings: Clutch.co, UpCity, Google/Google Maps, LinkedIn recommendations, Baltimore Business Journal awards, PRSA/AMA local chapters.  
4. Vet the team: who will do the work vs. who pitches? Ask to meet the actual account/creative/analytics leads.  
5. Ask for references and call at least two clients with similar goals.  
6. Start with a time-boxed pilot (30–90 days) or a specific project before committing to a long retainer.  
7. Confirm reporting cadence, ownership of creative/assets, termination terms, and expected timelines to results.

Key interview questions to ask an agency
- Have you worked with clients like us? Can you share specific outcomes (metrics, before/after)?  
- Who on your team will work with us and what are their backgrounds?  
- What will a typical 90-day plan look like for our goals?  
- How do you measure performance and how often will you report?  
- What is your pricing model (retainer, project, performance-based, media spend markup)?  
- Can you provide 2–3 client references I can contact?

Red flags
- No measurable case studies or only vanity metrics.  
- Unwillingness to provide references or to show real work.  
- Promises of “guaranteed rankings” or “overnight results.”  
- Very high churn or unclear team assignments.

If you want, give me your industry, goals and budget and I’ll compile a short vetted list (3–6) of Maryland agencies that are a strong fit, plus pros/cons for each. Which details would you like to start with?
